title: A Library Reading Event
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a librarian who wanted more children to read. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a librarian noticed that very few children were visiting the library.
scenes: コマ1:図書館の子ども向けコーナーががらんとしている。司書の女性が残念そうに見ている。
コマ2:「A week later」。司書が「Story Time Every Saturday」というポスターを作り、学校に配っている。
コマ3:「That Saturday」。たくさんの子どもが集まり、司書の読み聞かせを楽しそうに聞いている。
コマ4:「A few weeks later」。人が多すぎて部屋に入りきらず、子どもや親が廊下に立っている。司書が困った顔をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a librarian noticed that very few children were visiting the library. The children's corner was almost empty. A week later, she made posters about a story time every Saturday and handed them out at local schools. That Saturday, many children came to the library and enjoyed listening to her read stories. A few weeks later, however, so many children and parents came that the room was too small, and some people had to stand in the hallway. The librarian looked worried.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the librarian, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm glad the event is so popular, but it's not safe to have so many people here. Maybe we should hold two sessions or ask people to register in advance."

questions.question: Do you think young people read fewer books than in the past?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Young people spend a lot of time on smartphones and video sites. However, many of them read online articles and e-books, so they may be reading in different ways.

questions.question: Should public libraries offer more services than just lending books?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they should. Libraries can be community centers that offer study spaces, computer classes, and events for different age groups. This would encourage more people to use them.

title: An Electric Car
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a couple who bought a new car. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a couple was looking at their gas bill and the price of gasoline.
scenes: コマ1:夫婦がガソリン代のレシートを見て、高いことに驚いている。
コマ2:「A few weeks later」。夫婦が販売店で電気自動車を選んでいる。販売員が説明している。
コマ3:「A month later」。夫婦が自宅で車を充電しながら、満足そうにしている。
コマ4:「On a long trip」。高速道路の充電スタンドに長い列ができていて、夫婦がいらいらしながら待っている。
narrationSample: One day, a couple was looking at their receipts for gasoline and was surprised at how expensive it had become. A few weeks later, they were choosing an electric car at a car dealer, and a salesperson was explaining its features. A month later, the couple was charging the car at home and looked very satisfied. However, when they went on a long trip, there was a long line at a charging station on the highway, and the couple became frustrated while waiting.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the husband, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I didn't expect to wait this long. Next time, we should plan our trip more carefully and check where the charging stations are in advance."

questions.question: Do you think electric cars will become more common in Japan?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Electric cars are better for the environment, and their prices are gradually falling. As the number of charging stations increases, more people will choose them.

questions.question: Should the government ban the sale of new gasoline cars in the future?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think it's a good goal, but it should be done carefully. The government needs to make sure there are enough charging stations and that electric cars are affordable. Otherwise, people in rural areas may have trouble getting around.

title: A Part-Time Job
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a student who got a part-time job. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a high school student wanted to buy a new guitar.
scenes: コマ1:楽器店で男子高校生が高いギターの値札を見て、ため息をついている。
コマ2:「The next week」。男子生徒がレストランでアルバイトを始め、皿を運んでいる。
コマ3:「A few months later」。男子生徒がお金を貯めてギターを買い、うれしそうに弾いている。
コマ4:「At school」。テストの答案に低い点数が書かれていて、男子生徒が肩を落としている。先生が心配そうに見ている。
narrationSample: One day, a high school student wanted to buy a new guitar, but when he saw the price at a music store, he sighed. The next week, he started working part-time at a restaurant, carrying dishes to customers. A few months later, he had saved enough money to buy the guitar, and he was happily playing it. However, at school, he received a test with a low score, and he looked very disappointed. His teacher looked worried about him.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the student, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I've been working too much and haven't had enough time to study. I need to reduce my working hours and focus on my studies before the next exam."

questions.question: Do you think high school students should have part-time jobs?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think it can be a good experience. Students can learn about responsibility and the value of money. However, they should not work so much that it affects their studies.

questions.question: Should young people be taught more about managing money at school?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Many young people don't know how to save money or avoid debt. If they learn about personal finance at school, they will be better prepared for adult life.

title: A Rainy Day Event
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman who planned an outdoor event. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a woman was asked to plan her company's summer barbecue.
scenes: コマ1:上司が女性に「Company Barbecue — Planner」と書かれた紙を渡している。
コマ2:「A few weeks later」。女性が公園の予約や食材の準備をしている。
コマ3:「On the morning of the event」。空が曇り、雨が降り始めている。女性が窓の外を見て心配そう。
コマ4:「That afternoon」。会社の会議室でホットプレートを使って焼き肉をしながら、社員たちが楽しそうにしている。女性はほっとした表情。
narrationSample: One day, a woman's boss asked her to plan the company's summer barbecue. A few weeks later, she was busy reserving a place in the park and preparing food. On the morning of the event, however, the sky was cloudy and it started to rain. She looked out the window and was worried. That afternoon, the employees were cooking meat on hot plates in a meeting room at the company instead. Everyone was enjoying themselves, and the woman looked relieved.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm so relieved that everyone is having fun even though it rained. It was a good idea to have a backup plan."

questions.question: Do you think company events help employees work better together?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they do. Events give employees a chance to talk with colleagues from other departments in a relaxed atmosphere. This can improve communication at work.

questions.question: Should companies give employees more paid holidays?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Japanese workers often work long hours and don't take many holidays. More holidays would help them rest and could actually make them more productive.

title: A Second-Hand Shop
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman who cleaned her house. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a woman was looking at her closet full of clothes she never wore.
scenes: コマ1:女性がクローゼットいっぱいの着ていない服を見てため息をついている。
コマ2:「That weekend」。女性が服を袋に詰め、リサイクルショップに持ち込んでいる。
コマ3:「A week later」。女性がすっきりした部屋で、受け取ったお金を見て満足している。
コマ4:「A month later」。女性がショッピングモールで、新しい服をたくさん買って紙袋を抱えている。友人があきれた顔で見ている。
narrationSample: One day, a woman was looking at her closet full of clothes that she never wore, and she sighed. That weekend, she put the clothes into bags and took them to a second-hand shop. A week later, she was sitting in her tidy room and looked satisfied with the money she had received. However, a month later, she was at a shopping mall carrying many bags of new clothes. Her friend looked at her in disbelief.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the friend, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "She just sold all her old clothes, and now she's buying more. She should think more carefully about what she really needs before shopping."

questions.question: Do you think people today buy more things than they need?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Online shopping and cheap products make it easy to buy things without thinking. Many people end up with things they rarely use.

questions.question: Should companies be responsible for recycling the products they sell?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. If companies are responsible for recycling, they will design products that last longer and are easier to recycle. This would reduce waste.

title: A Hospital Volunteer
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a retired man who wanted to do something useful. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a retired man was sitting at home with nothing to do.
scenes: コマ1:退職した男性がソファで退屈そうにテレビを見ている。
コマ2:「A few days later」。男性が新聞で「Hospital Volunteers Wanted」という記事を見つけて関心を持っている。
コマ3:「A month later」。男性が病院で、高齢の患者の車いすを押しながら楽しそうに話している。
コマ4:「That evening」。男性が疲れて帰宅し、腰を押さえている。妻が心配そうに見ている。
narrationSample: One day, a retired man was sitting at home with nothing to do. He was watching TV on the sofa and looked bored. A few days later, he found an article in the newspaper about a hospital looking for volunteers, and he became interested. A month later, he was pushing an elderly patient's wheelchair at the hospital and chatting happily with him. That evening, however, he came home exhausted and was holding his back. His wife looked worried about him.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the wife, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm glad he has found something meaningful to do, but he shouldn't work too hard. He should ask the hospital for lighter tasks."

questions.question: Do you think elderly people should continue working after retirement age?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, if they want to and are healthy enough. Working can help them stay active and connected to society. Their experience is also valuable for younger workers.

questions.question: Should hospitals rely more on volunteers?
questions.sampleAnswer: Volunteers can be very helpful, for example by guiding patients or talking with them. However, hospitals should not rely on volunteers for important medical work, which must be done by trained professionals.

title: A Bakery's Online Shop
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a couple who ran a bakery. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a couple who ran a small bakery noticed that fewer customers were coming to their shop.
scenes: コマ1:パン屋の店内に客がいなく、夫婦が売れ残ったパンを見てため息をついている。
コマ2:「A few weeks later」。夫婦がパソコンでネットショップのページを作っている。
コマ3:「A month later」。店の奥に注文の箱が山積みになり、夫婦が忙しく梱包している。
コマ4:「The next day」。客からの電話で、配送中にパンがつぶれたという苦情を受けて、夫婦が困った顔をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a couple who ran a small bakery noticed that fewer customers were coming to their shop, and they sighed as they looked at the unsold bread. A few weeks later, they were creating an online shop on their computer. A month later, there were piles of orders in the back of the shop, and the couple was busy packing boxes. However, the next day, they received a phone call from a customer complaining that the bread had been crushed during delivery. The couple looked troubled.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the husband, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "We need to apologize to the customer and send a new order. We should also find better packaging so that the bread doesn't get damaged."

questions.question: Do you think online shopping will replace shopping in stores?
questions.sampleAnswer: I don't think it will replace stores completely. Online shopping is convenient, but many people still enjoy seeing and touching products before buying them. Stores also provide a place for people to meet and talk.

questions.question: Should the government do more to help small businesses?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Small businesses create jobs and give character to local communities. The government could offer low-interest loans or help them use digital technology.

title: Moving to the Countryside
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a family who moved from the city to the countryside. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a father was riding a crowded train to work.
scenes: コマ1:満員電車で父親が押しつぶされそうになり、疲れた顔をしている。
コマ2:「A few months later」。家族が田舎の家に引っ越し、広い庭を見て喜んでいる。
コマ3:「The next week」。父親が自宅でリモートワークをしながら、窓の外の山を眺めて満足そう。
コマ4:「That winter」。大雪で道が埋まり、家族が車を出せず、子どもが学校に行けないで困っている。
narrationSample: One day, a father was riding a crowded train to work, and he looked very tired. A few months later, the family had moved to a house in the countryside, and they were delighted with the large garden. The next week, the father was working from home and looking out the window at the mountains with satisfaction. However, that winter, heavy snow covered the road. The family could not take their car out, and the children could not go to school.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the father, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Life in the countryside is wonderful, but we weren't prepared for this much snow. We should buy a snow shovel and talk to our neighbors about how they deal with winter."

questions.question: Do you think more people will move from cities to rural areas in the future?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Remote work has made it possible for many people to live away from their offices. Rural areas also offer cheaper housing and a more relaxed lifestyle.

questions.question: Should the government do more to stop the population decline in rural areas?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think it should. If rural areas lose their populations, schools and hospitals will close, and it will become even harder to live there. The government should support jobs and transportation in these areas.

title: A Language Exchange
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who wanted to improve his English. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a man was trying to talk to a foreign colleague at work.
scenes: コマ1:職場で男性が外国人の同僚に話しかけようとしているが、言葉が出ず困っている。
コマ2:「A few days later」。男性がカフェで、日本語を学びたい外国人と言語交換をしている。
コマ3:「A few months later」。男性が会議で英語を使って自信を持って発表している。
コマ4:「The next week」。上司が男性に海外支社への転勤を伝え、男性は驚いた顔をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a man was trying to talk to a foreign colleague at work, but he could not find the right words. A few days later, he was doing a language exchange at a café with a foreigner who wanted to learn Japanese. A few months later, he was giving a presentation in English at a meeting with confidence. The next week, his boss told him that he was being transferred to an overseas branch, and the man looked very surprised.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "This is a great opportunity, but it's a big change. I need to talk with my family and prepare myself for living in another country."

questions.question: Do you think it is important for Japanese people to learn English?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. English is used around the world in business and on the internet. Being able to speak English gives people more opportunities in their careers and helps them understand other cultures.

questions.question: Should companies send more young employees to work overseas?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Working overseas helps young employees develop language skills and a global perspective. These experiences are valuable for companies that do business internationally.

title: A Community Clean-Up
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who went jogging by the river. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a man was jogging along the river near his home.
scenes: コマ1:川沿いをジョギングしている男性が、河原に散らかったごみを見て顔をしかめている。
コマ2:「That weekend」。男性がインターネットで清掃ボランティアを募集している。
コマ3:「The next Sunday」。たくさんの住民が集まり、川沿いのごみを拾っている。
コマ4:「A few weeks later」。きれいになった河原で、テレビ局が男性にインタビューしており、男性は照れくさそうにしている。
narrationSample: One day, a man was jogging along the river near his home when he noticed a lot of trash on the riverbank. He frowned at the sight. That weekend, he posted a message on the internet looking for volunteers to clean up the river. The next Sunday, many local residents gathered and picked up the trash along the river. A few weeks later, the riverbank was clean, and a TV station was interviewing the man. He looked a little embarrassed.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm a little embarrassed to be on TV, but I hope this interview will encourage more people to help keep our river clean."

questions.question: Do you think social media is a good way to solve local problems?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think it can be. Social media makes it easy to share information and gather volunteers quickly. However, people should be careful because false information can also spread quickly.

questions.question: Should people who litter in public places be fined?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Fines would make people think twice before throwing trash on the street. The money could also be used to keep public places clean.

title: A New Coworking Space
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman who worked as a freelance designer. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a freelance designer was working at home and feeling lonely.
scenes: コマ1:女性が自宅で一人パソコンに向かい、さびしそうな顔をしている。
コマ2:「The next week」。女性がコワーキングスペースの見学に来て、明るい雰囲気に感心している。
コマ3:「A few months later」。女性がコワーキングスペースで知り合った人たちと、一緒にプロジェクトの打ち合わせをしている。
コマ4:「At the end of the month」。女性が会費の請求書を見て驚いている。電卓で計算している。
narrationSample: One day, a freelance designer was working alone at home and feeling lonely. The next week, she visited a coworking space and was impressed by its bright and friendly atmosphere. A few months later, she was having a meeting about a project with people she had met at the coworking space. However, at the end of the month, she was surprised when she looked at the bill for the membership fee, and she started calculating her expenses.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "The fee is more expensive than I expected. But I've made useful connections here, so maybe I can choose a cheaper plan and come only a few days a week."

questions.question: Do you think more people will become freelancers in the future?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. The internet makes it easy to find work and communicate with clients. Many people also want more freedom in choosing when and how they work.

questions.question: Should the government provide more support for freelance workers?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think it should. Freelancers often don't have the same protections as company employees, such as paid leave or unemployment benefits. The government should create systems to support them.

title: A Disaster Drill
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a mother who worried about earthquakes. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a mother was watching a news report about a large earthquake.
scenes: コマ1:母親がテレビで大地震のニュースを見て、心配そうな顔をしている。
コマ2:「That weekend」。母親と子どもたちが防災用品(水、懐中電灯、非常食)を買いそろえている。
コマ3:「A month later」。地域の避難訓練に家族で参加し、子どもたちが真剣に説明を聞いている。
コマ4:「Half a year later」。母親が非常用の袋を開けると、非常食の賞味期限が切れていて、困った顔をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a mother was watching a news report about a large earthquake, and she became worried. That weekend, she and her children bought emergency supplies such as water, flashlights, and emergency food. A month later, the family took part in a local disaster drill, and the children listened carefully to the instructions. Half a year later, however, the mother opened the emergency bag and found that the emergency food had passed its expiration date. She looked troubled.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the mother, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I should have checked the expiration dates regularly. From now on, I'll check our emergency supplies every few months and replace old food."

questions.question: Do you think people in Japan are well prepared for natural disasters?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think many people are better prepared than in the past, but not enough. Some people still don't have emergency supplies or know where to evacuate. More education and regular drills are needed.

questions.question: Should companies be required to prepare for disasters?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Companies are responsible for the safety of their employees. They should store emergency supplies and have plans so that they can continue important work after a disaster.
